sourceItems.name: Traditional PTFE / Teflon Non-Stick Skillet
currentRisks: Sheds 9,100 to 2.3M microplastic & nanoplastic particles per scratch (Flinders Univ, 2022)
Degrades at >260°C (500°F) releasing toxic fluoropolymer pyrolysis fumes (Polymer Fume Fever)
Frequent replacement cycle (12-24 months) generating recurring household landfill waste
sourceItems.primaryToxins: PTFE, PFOA/PFHxA traces, PFAS oligomers, fluorinated pyrolysis gas

sourceItems.name: Degraded / Chipped Sol-Gel Ceramic Pan
currentRisks: Loss of non-stick silica matrix leading to food burning and stubborn carbon buildup
Micro-fractures harbor degraded cooking oils and potential substrate metal migration
Cheap non-certified imports may contain unbonded lead or cadmium glazes beneath topcoat
sourceItems.primaryToxins: Exposed aluminum substrate ions, micro-silica particulate, degraded oils

sourceItems.name: Bare / Unanodized Aluminum Pot or Sheet Pan
currentRisks: Acidic ingredients (tomatoes, wine, citrus) leach 20-50 mg of aluminum ions per meal
Gray oxidation smudging and metallic flavor contamination in delicate foods
Exceeds EFSA tolerable weekly intake of 1 mg/kg body weight under acidic simmering
sourceItems.primaryToxins: Aluminum ions (Al³⁺), aluminum oxide smudges, reactive galvanic salts

sourceItems.name: Plastic Food Storage & Reheating Containers
currentRisks: Microwave reheating causes polymer scission, leaching billions of nanoplastics per cm²
Lipophilic food absorption pulls plasticizers, phthalates, and bisphenol analogs into fatty foods
Permanent greasy film, stubborn tomato staining, and micro-cracking over time
sourceItems.primaryToxins: Microplastics, nanoplastics, phthalates, BPA/BPS analogs, cyclic oligomers

sourceItems.name: Plastic Cutting Board (Polypropylene / HDPE)
currentRisks: Knife incisions shave off 15 to 50 million microplastic particles per board per year (ACS, 2023)
Deep knife grooves harbor pathogenic bacteria (Salmonella, E. coli) that resist dishwasher sanitize cycles
Microplastics adhere directly to chopped vegetables, poultry, and meat
sourceItems.primaryToxins: Polyethylene & polypropylene micro-shavings, bacterial biofilm deep in knife scars

sourceItems.name: Coated Non-Stick Baking Pans & Roasting Trays
currentRisks: High baking temperatures (400°F-450°F) approach coating thermal decomposition threshold
Coating chips around rolled rims and corners flake invisibly into cakes and breads
Metal spatulas and cookie cutters severely scratch non-stick layers
sourceItems.primaryToxins: PTFE flakes, fluorinated baking fumes, charred cooking fat bound to fluoropolymers

sourceItems.name: Unlined Vintage Copper Pan / Kettle
currentRisks: Acidic or salty ingredients corrode unlined copper forming toxic copper salts (verdigris / copper acetate)
Induces acute copper toxicity: nausea, vomiting, abdominal cramping, and hepatic stress
Requires constant polishing and strict avoidance of all acidic recipes
sourceItems.primaryToxins: Copper ions (Cu²⁺), copper acetate (verdigris), heavy metal toxicity

sourceItems.name: Melamine Formaldehyde Dinnerware & Kids' Bowls
currentRisks: Hot foods (>70°C / 160°F) or microwave heating accelerate migration of formaldehyde monomers
Chronic exposure linked to renal stones, kidney tubular damage, and bladder irritation
Brittle material easily micro-cracks and absorbs stains
sourceItems.primaryToxins: Formaldehyde, melamine monomer, cyanuric acid condensation byproducts

materials.name: 18/10 (304) or 316 Marine Stainless Steel
materials.chemicalProfile: Completely non-porous chromium oxide passive layer. Zero PTFE, PFOA, GenX, lead, cadmium, or petroleum sealants.
materials.bestFor: High-heat searing, deglazing pan sauces, acidic tomato reductions, boiling, broiling, everyday cooking.
materials.tradeOffs: Requires learning the Leidenfrost water-drop preheating method to prevent delicate eggs and fish from sticking. Trace nickel leaching during first 2-3 acidic cooks (only relevant to severe nickel allergy sufferers).
materials.maintenance: Dishwasher safe; Bar Keepers Friend restores mirror finish easily.
materials.learningCurve: Medium (Master the 2-minute preheat test for naturally non-stick frying)

materials.name: Pure Pre-Seasoned Cast Iron
materials.chemicalProfile: 100% natural polymerized plant oil (soy, flaxseed, or sunflower) cross-linked to iron crystal lattice. Zero synthetic chemicals. Fortifies food with beneficial dietary iron (Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺).
materials.bestFor: Steak searing, smash burgers, cornbread, deep frying, Dutch baby pancakes, campfire cooking.
materials.tradeOffs: Heavy weight; hand-wash only (never dishwasher); acidic stews simmered >1 hour can strip the seasoning patina.
materials.maintenance: Rinse with hot water & brush, dry immediately, wipe with a drop of cooking oil.
materials.learningCurve: Low-to-Medium (Requires simple hand drying and occasional oil wipe)

materials.name: Blue / Black Carbon Steel
materials.badge: The Chef's Secret Lightweight Wok & Skillet
materials.chemicalProfile: 99% iron and 1% carbon with natural polymerized oil seasoning. Identical non-toxic chemistry to cast iron at half the weight.
materials.bestFor: Stir-frying, high-heat searing, crispy fried eggs, crepes, fish fillets, wok cookery.
materials.tradeOffs: Hand-wash only; reactive to prolonged acidic tomato simmering; arrives with protective beeswax that must be washed before first seasoning.
materials.maintenance: Hand-wash without harsh detergents, dry thoroughly on warm stovetop burner.
materials.learningCurve: Medium (Initial seasoning ritual required; builds glass-smooth black patina over time)

materials.name: Vitreous Enameled Cast Iron
materials.chemicalProfile: Inorganic vitreous porcelain glass fused to cast iron at 1400°F (760°C). 100% non-reactive, acid-proof, lead-free and cadmium-free in certified reputable brands.
materials.bestFor: Slow braises, 12-hour marinara and bolognese sauces, sourdough boules, soups, stews, pot roasts.
materials.tradeOffs: Heavy; enamel can chip if dropped or subjected to extreme thermal shock (plunging hot pot into ice water); premium price point.
materials.maintenance: Warm water and sponge; safe for gentle dishwashing though hand washing preserves glossy finish.
materials.learningCurve: Low (Cooks like traditional cookware without any seasoning needed)

materials.name: 100% Sol-Gel Mineral Ceramic (PTFE-Free)
materials.chemicalProfile: Inorganic silicon dioxide (SiO₂) sand sol-gel matrix. 100% free from PTFE, PFOA, PFOS, PFAS, lead, and cadmium.
materials.bestFor: Low-to-medium heat delicate eggs, pancakes, delicate fish, quick omelets with zero oil.
materials.tradeOffs: Shorter functional lifespan than stainless or cast iron; surface microscopic pores degrade after 2-4 years; strictly hand-wash only; aerosol oil sprays prohibited.
materials.maintenance: Soft sponge and mild dish soap only; avoid high heat and aerosol propellant sprays.
materials.learningCurve: Very Low (Immediate effortless release; gentle heat management required)

materials.name: Pure High-Thermal Borosilicate Glass
materials.chemicalProfile: 80% silica, 13% boric oxide. Zero chemical migration, zero staining, zero odor retention. Withstands extreme thermal shock ΔT of 150°C (270°F).
materials.bestFor: Meal prep storage, microwave reheating, oven casseroles, lasagna, acid-heavy food refrigeration.
materials.tradeOffs: Cannot be used on stovetop direct burner; fragile if dropped onto concrete or ceramic tile floor.
materials.maintenance: 100% dishwasher, freezer, microwave, and oven safe.
materials.learningCurve: Zero (Effortless daily use; stain-proof and odor-proof)

materials.name: End-Grain Hardwood (Maple / Walnut / Larch)
materials.chemicalProfile: Natural sustained hardwood bonded with FDA-approved food-safe glue. Natural wood tannins and polyphenols provide inherent antimicrobial defense. Zero synthetic microplastics.
materials.bestFor: Daily knife chopping, vegetable slicing, meat carving, bread cutting.
materials.tradeOffs: Never put in dishwasher or submerge in water; requires monthly food-grade mineral oil or beeswax conditioning.
materials.maintenance: Hand wipe with soapy damp cloth, towel dry immediately, apply mineral oil monthly.
materials.learningCurve: Low (Gentle rinse and quick monthly oil conditioning preserves it for decades)

materials.name: 100% Platinum-Cured Food-Grade Silicone
materials.chemicalProfile: Silicon-oxygen elastomer cured with high-purity platinum catalyst. Zero peroxide byproducts, zero BPA, BPS, phthalates, or lead.
materials.bestFor: Freezer meal storage, sous vide cooking, microwave steaming, reusable sandwich bags, baking mats.
materials.tradeOffs: Can absorb strong aromatic spice odors (curry, garlic) if not washed promptly; floppy structure compared to rigid glass.
materials.maintenance: Dishwasher safe; boil in baking soda water for 10 minutes to eliminate stubborn food aromas.
